name: Tyrosine supplements for tanning
lead: Tyrosine supplements for tanning refers to the practice of taking L-tyrosine, a standard amino acid, as pills or applying it in lotions with the aim of darkening skin or speeding a tan. The idea rests on tyrosine's role as a building block of melanin, the pigment produced by melanocytes [1][2].

Tyrosine is a conditionally essential amino acid that the body makes from phenylalanine and obtains from protein-rich foods; it is also sold as a dietary supplement [1]. Published research on supplemental tyrosine has focused on effects on neurotransmitters and performance under stress rather than on pigmentation [1].
No human trials of tyrosine as a tanning aid were located. The only trial record linked to the entry in the research database is unrelated to the topic (an oncology study).
infobox: Meat, fish, dairy, eggs, some nuts and seeds [1]

paras: Tyrosine is one of the 20 standard amino acids and a precursor of melanin, as well as of neurotransmitters such as dopamine and norepinephrine [1]. Melanocytes make melanin, which absorbs ultraviolet radiation, and tanning involves increased melanin production after UV exposure [2].

Supplement marketing for tanning commonly points to this biochemical role, suggesting that extra substrate could support more pigment. Whether additional dietary or topical tyrosine changes skin pigmentation in people with normal tyrosine intake has not been established in published trials.

No studies found. Research on supplemental tyrosine in healthy people has examined cognition and mood under demanding conditions, with a 2015 systematic review concluding it may benefit working memory under stress [1]. That research did not study skin pigmentation.

Supplemental tyrosine is widely sold as a dietary supplement [1]. Any tanning use does not remove the need for UV exposure for tanning to occur, and the health risks of UV exposure, including skin cancer, are documented separately [2].

card.summary: Amino-acid pills or lotion sold on the idea that more raw material means more melanin, with no human tanning trials behind it.
card.note: Tyrosine does not replace UV exposure for tanning; UV exposure carries skin cancer risk.

quick.overview:
L-tyrosine is a common amino acid and a building block of melanin. Some tanning products and supplement sellers suggest taking it orally or applying it topically to boost tanning.

No published human studies have tested whether it changes tanning or skin colour.
quick.mechanism: Melanocytes convert tyrosine into melanin after UV exposure. Proponents reason that extra tyrosine supplies more raw material; research has not tested whether this changes pigment in people.
quick.risks: Tyrosine is sold as a dietary supplement. Tanning itself involves UV exposure, which is classified as a carcinogen and causes sunburn and skin ageing.
